answer.rationale: Switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor directly addresses the 18% cost-cut mandate since the incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle. Memory c2 records that a prior switch to the low-cost vendor was quick to onboard, invoicing stayed accurate, and unit cost was sharply cut; verification would confirm the operational details. Memory c3 shows that a second-source buffer previously protected the line during shortages, so I flag the loss of the incumbent's integration depth as a delivery-risk exposure to be mitigated at the next review cycle. The assembly line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so the switch must include a contractual delivery-SLA with penalties and an agreed transition overlap window; memory c2's onboarding evidence supports a short transition. No incumbent price path remains (memory c6's multi-year volume pricing is not on the table this cycle, memory c1's renewal benefit is moot given the incumbent's stance), so deferring or negotiating terms would not meet the finance mandate within the 14-day expiry.
